title: Supported perfect restriction data on a compact-open overlap model
statement: Let $X$ be a quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme], $W$ a compact open and $V$ an affine open, and let $T\subseteq X$ be closed with compact complement. Choose derived localizations [def-pc-derived-category] with common Hom universe $w$ on $W,V$, their localized open sites, and $W\cap V$. Let $F\in D(\mathcal O_W)$ be perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex] with every cohomology stalk vanishing outside $T$. Write $S_W,S_V$ for transported overlap restriction [def-pc-derived-open-restriction-maps]. There exist a compact open $U\subseteq V$, chosen derived localizations on $U$ and every localized open site of $U$ in universe $w$, and a perfect $G\in D(\mathcal O_U)$ such that the inverse image $T_V$ of $T$ in $V$ is closed with compact complement and every cohomology stalk of $G$ vanishes outside the inverse image of $T_V$. There is an equivalence $e:D(\mathcal O_U)\simeq D(\mathcal O_{W\cap V})$, a natural isomorphism $J_U\mathbin{\ggg}e\cong S_V$, and an isomorphism $e(G\oplus G[1])\cong S_W(F\oplus F[1])$. No object on all of $V$ and no morphism lifting is asserted.

proof.text:
Set U to the open range of the inclusion of W intersect V into V. The intersection
is compact by quasi-separatedness and compactness of W and affine V, so U is compact.
The inverse image of T in V is closed. Its complement identifies through the open
embedding with V intersect the compact open complement of T, hence is compact by the
same intersection criterion. The inclusion U.toScheme into W is an open immersion.
Define G by exact restriction of F along that inclusion. At each point of U, pull back
a strictly perfect neighbourhood model of F, preserving the degree bounds, finite free
modules and retract equations. These give perfectness of G. Exact homology and the
restriction-stalk comparison identify each stalk of G with the corresponding stalk of F,
so support restricts as stated. The scheme isomorphism from the ambient overlap to U
supplies the exact module equivalence and the derived equivalence e. Transport the
chosen derived localization along it, and transport the localized-site localizations
through the corresponding equivalences on each open of U to supply hO. The natural
restriction composition comparisons identify ordinary restriction from V followed by e
with SV, and identify e(G) with SW(F). Both comparisons arise by deriving the underived
restriction comparisons, so commute with shifts and biproducts. Apply those comparisons
to G plus G[1] to obtain the last isomorphism. Empty opens and empty support need no
separate case: the same scheme isomorphism, exact restrictions and zero stalks apply.

mathlib_searches.query: Restriction to an open subscheme preserves locally perfect complexes and vanishing homology stalks; affine supported extension plus shift
A perfect complex restricts to a perfect complex on an open subscheme; the direct sum with its shift has the same closed support.
